benchmark.name: CCURE Windows Hardening Baseline
benchmark.notes: Generated by scripts/benchmarks/build_baseline_packs.py from the built-in rules in core/config_audit/builtin/. Not a CIS Benchmark. Crosswalk targets are CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1 safeguards.

profiles.title: Level 1 — settings a general-purpose host should meet
Level 2 — defence in depth, may affect usability

controls.description: The local security policy's minimum password length.
controls.rationale: Length is the property that most directly resists offline cracking of a recovered hash.
controls.remediation: Set Minimum password length to 14 or more in the local security policy, or through the domain password policy where the host is joined.
controls.title: Minimum password length is at least 14 characters

controls.description: How many previous passwords the system refuses to accept again.
controls.rationale: Without history a forced change can be satisfied by re-setting the password that was just compromised.
controls.remediation: Set 'Enforce password history' to 24 or more.
controls.title: Password history retains at least 24 passwords

controls.description: Failed sign-in attempts before the account is locked.
controls.rationale: A per-account lockout is the control that answers credential stuffing from many source addresses, which no per-address rate limit can.
controls.remediation: Set 'Account lockout threshold' to a value between 1 and 10, with a lockout duration long enough to make automated guessing impractical.
controls.title: Account lockout threshold is set and workable

controls.description: User Account Control mediates elevation to administrative rights. With it off, any process started by a member of the local Administrators group runs fully elevated with no prompt and no split token.
controls.rationale: Disabling UAC removes the boundary that stops a single user-context compromise becoming immediate administrative control of the machine.
controls.remediation: Set EnableLUA to 1 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System and restart the host.
controls.title: User Account Control is enabled

controls.description: Controls whether an unauthenticated session may enumerate local account names.
controls.rationale: An account list is the input to password spraying; withholding it removes the step that makes spraying efficient.
controls.title: Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts is restricted

controls.description: The SMB version 1 server protocol, superseded since 2006 and the transport used by EternalBlue and WannaCry.
controls.rationale: SMBv1 has no protocol-level integrity protection and cannot negotiate the mitigations later dialects carry.
controls.remediation: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol, or set SMB1 to 0 under the LanmanServer parameters key.
controls.title: SMBv1 server is disabled

controls.description: The Telnet server service, which carries credentials in clear text.
controls.rationale: Telnet authenticates over an unencrypted channel; anyone able to observe the path recovers the password.
controls.remediation: Uninstall the Telnet Server feature and use SSH or WinRM over HTTPS instead.
controls.title: Telnet server is not installed

controls.description: Network Level Authentication makes the client authenticate before a Remote Desktop session is created.
controls.rationale: Without NLA the server allocates a session and renders a logon screen to an unauthenticated caller, which both widens the pre-authentication attack surface and makes RDP usable for resource exhaustion.
controls.remediation: Enable 'Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication', or set UserAuthentication to 1 on the RDP-Tcp listener.
controls.title: RDP requires Network Level Authentication

controls.description: The Remote Registry service allows the registry to be read and written across the network.
controls.rationale: It is rarely required on a workstation and gives an authenticated attacker a broad configuration read, and often a write.
controls.remediation: Stop the RemoteRegistry service and set its start type to Disabled where remote management does not depend on it.
controls.title: Remote Registry service is not running

controls.description: The Windows Defender Firewall service enforces host packet filtering.
controls.rationale: With the service stopped, every profile's rules are inert and the host accepts whatever the network offers it.
controls.remediation: Start-Service MpsSvc and set its start type to Automatic.
controls.title: Windows Firewall service is running

controls.description: Windows advanced audit policy decides which security events reach the event log at all.
controls.rationale: Without the subcategories configured, an investigation has no record of the actions it is trying to reconstruct.
controls.remediation: Configure Advanced Audit Policy Configuration under Security Settings, and set the audit subcategories your logging standard requires.
controls.title: Advanced audit policy subcategories are configured
controls.unimplemented_reason: auditpol output is collected as free text and is not yet parsed into per-subcategory settings, so no expected state can be compared against it.
